title: Extraction of caffeine from natural matter using a bio-renewable agrochemical solvent
author: Villanueva Bermejo, David
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Prepare plant material
steps.instruction: Obtain green coffee beans and green tea leaves to be used as the source material for caffeine extraction.

steps.title: Load ASE cell with sample and solvent
steps.instruction: Place the plant material into the Accelerated Solvent Extraction (ASE) cell and add ethyl lactate (ethyl 2‑hydroxy‑propanoate) as the extraction solvent.

steps.title: Run static extraction at specified temperature
steps.instruction: Set the ASE system to static extraction mode for a single 10‑minute step and perform the extraction at each of the three temperatures—100 °C, 150 °C, and 200 °C—using identical conditions for each run.

substeps.instruction: Set temperature to 100 °C and extract for 10 min
Set temperature to 150 °C and extract for 10 min
Set temperature to 200 °C and extract for 10 min

steps.title: Analyze extracts and compare recoveries
steps.instruction: Collect the extracts, determine the extraction yield and caffeine recovery, and compare these results with extracts obtained using ethyl acetate or ethanol; note that ethyl lactate gave an approximate 60 % caffeine recovery.
